alive.last_commit_message:
fix(cli): honor --stderr-file for config and known-configs scans (#287)

* fix(cli): pass --stderr-file to config and known-configs scans

--stderr-file was only applied to the stdio subcommand and the legacy
--stdio-command path. Config file scans (config, known-configs and the
legacy --config-path / --scan-known-configs flags) also spawn stdio
servers but ignored it, so their stderr always went to the terminal.

Open the file once and pass it as errlog to scan_mcp_config_file and
scan_well_known_mcp_configs, and accept --stderr-file on the config and
known-configs subcommands. A top-level --stderr-file given before the
subcommand keeps working.

Add unit tests for errlog passthrough in Scanner._get_stdio_session,
its sys.stderr default, and the CLI config scan paths.

Refs #69

* fix(cli): keep a leading --stderr-file on the stdio subcommand

The stdio subparser's --stderr-file defaulted to None, so
`mcp-scanner --stderr-file server.log stdio ...` dropped the top-level
value. Use argparse.SUPPRESS, matching config and known-configs, and
keep reading the attribute with getattr so a missing flag stays None.

Add a regression test for both flag orders and an offline config-file
scan that checks a real stdio server's startup stderr lands in the
file rather than the terminal.

Co-authored-by: Jonathan Di Rico <yonasuriv@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(test): do not close stdin before communicate() on Python 3.11

Python 3.11 flushes stdin inside Popen.communicate() and raises
ValueError: flush of closed file if the pipe was already closed.
That is not an OSError, so the preflight helper would error.
communicate() closes stdin itself, so drop the manual close.

Signed-off-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
